notes.summary: Reconstructed bounded actual-type energy and exactly scoped foundations; no prior proof or review verdict is assumed.
notes.detailedSummary: For every connected compact Kähler n-fold, pseudoeffective zero-volume class and actual theta-psh reference, proves form-independent actual degree d<n, mixed degree>d vanishing, bounded cocycle/concavity, class-polynomial leading energy and representative/gauge invariance. Exact BEGZ, DDNL, Vu, DGMS and capacity hypotheses are stated, source convention and defects checked. This reconstruction is supporting material, not original-atom closure.
notes.text:
Only P15.1 is addressed. Let X be a connected smooth compact Kähler n-fold, α=[θ] pseudoeffective with vol(α)=0, and ψ an actual θ-psh reference. Set T_u=θ+ddᶜu, P=T_ψ, and C_ψ={u:ψ−C≤u≤ψ+C for some finite C}, using extended-valued inequalities. Our convention is ddᶜ=i∂∂̄/(2π). The retained data are actual bounded singularity type and an energy anchor.

The precise external foundations used are these. BEGZ, Acta Math. 205 (2010), arXiv:0812.3674v2, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4,1.6 and Theorem 1.8 give finite closed positive nonpluripolar products of closed positive (1,1) currents on compact Kähler X, positive-sum multilinearity, symmetry, plurifine locality and no pluripolar trace mass; smooth factors are ordinary wedge factors. DDNL, Anal. PDE 11 (2018), Proposition 2.1 gives equality of top mixed masses for bounded-equivalent potentials in every slot; Theorem 2.4 gives scalar mass monotonicity when every reference potential is less singular. Their backgrounds are smooth real closed forms with pseudoeffective classes, without bigness or small-unbounded-locus assumptions. We fill unused current slots by smooth Kähler forms with zero potentials; every hypothesis is then satisfied. DDNL source potentials are u/(2π), so the actual currents and comparisons agree with our convention.

BEGZ Sections 1.3–1.4 and Definition 1.17 give minimal-singularity potentials in big classes, define their top mass as volume, and give the boundary limit vol(α+ελ)→vol(α) for Kähler λ. Actual top mass is at most this volume by DDNL, not automatically equal to it. For nef classes the positive product equals cup product.

Vu, arXiv:2005.13241v3, Proposition 2.1(iii), Lemmas 2.5–2.6 and Theorem 2.7: for closed positive R of bidegree (n−1,n−1) and bounded R-admissible dsh a,b, the intrinsic finite gradients exist, the diagonal is positive, and ∫b⟨ddᶜa·∧R⟩=∫a⟨ddᶜb·∧R⟩=−∫⟨db∧dᶜa·∧R⟩. Admissibility means the two quasi-psh representation poles have zero R trace mass. All R below are smooth or nonpluripolar products times smooth positive factors, so our bounded differences and smooth tests are admissible. Iteration identifies each signed insertion with the difference of the ordinary positive products. Vu's operators are twice ours and its potentials are u/2. Its intrinsic gradient is half ours; multiplying source IBP by two gives the displayed identity. The mandatory intrinsic formula is da∧dᶜa R=(1/2)ddᶜ(a²)R−a ddᶜa R. Printed repeated half-factor omissions are preserved in the literal annex, not used as definitions. The full argument includes the corrected cutoff check: for ζ_k=1+k⁻¹max(Σφ_j,−k), negative representations with ddᶜφ_j≥−Ω, one has ∫dζ_k∧dᶜζ_k R≤(4/k)∫ΩR; uniformly bounded truncated differences have uniformly bounded gradient mass. Cauchy–Schwarz eliminates cutoff boundary terms. Only the nonzero cutoff locus, not its closed support, is asserted to lie in the strict truncation sets.

DGMS, Invent. Math. 29 (1975), Lemma 5.11 and Remark 5.14, imply that cohomologous smooth real closed (1,1) forms on compact Kähler X differ by ddᶜ of a smooth real function. Pure type makes the form d- and dᶜ-closed; its degree-two exactness supplies a degree-zero real primitive. These are exactly our representative-change hypotheses.

Define M_k(ψ,[ω])=∫⟨P^k⟩ω^(n−k), with empty product 1, and d=max{k:M_k>0}, m=n−d. Fixed Kähler forms are pointwise comparable, and positive power differences imply c^(n−k)M_k(ω)≤M_k(ω′)≤C^(n−k)M_k(ω). Thus d is form independent. Since P+εω≥εω, its class is big and its actual top mass is Σ_k binom(n,k)ε^(n−k)M_k≤vol(α+ε[ω])→0. Hence M_n=0 and d<n. DDNL, with n−k smooth slots, gives every bounded-type k-fold mixed trace mass M_k and bounds the corresponding more-singular mass by M_k. For k>d it is zero; positivity and domination of coefficient measures by the strictly positive trace imply vanishing as a current. Closedness and distributional Stokes make each M_k a homogeneous class polynomial.

For u,v in C_ψ define E_v,λ(u)=(d+1)⁻¹Σ_(a=0)^d∫(u−v)⟨T_u^aT_v^(d−a)⟩ω^m. To prove the cocycle, on any finite convex hull of bounded-type potentials write u_t=u_0+Σt_i h_i and A_i(t)=∫h_i⟨T_(u_t)^d⟩ω^m. These are finite polynomials. Signed differentiation and the checked bounded IBP with R=⟨T_(u_t)^(d−1)⟩ω^m give ∂_jA_i=∂_iA_j; at d=0 they are constant. Ordinary Stokes on a finite triangle proves path independence. The segment integral is the displayed energy because binom(d,a)∫₀¹t^a(1−t)^(d−a)dt=1/(d+1). Therefore E_ψ(u)−E_ψ(v)=E_v(u). Segment derivatives are ∫h⟨T_(u_t)^d⟩ω^m and second derivatives are −d times the positive intrinsic gradient mass, proving monotonicity and concavity. Constants give cM_d and the pointwise sandwich gives the M_d supremum-norm Lipschitz estimate. These differential claims concern finite hulls, not unbounded velocities.

Changing one of m complementary Kähler factors by ddᶜg, bounded IBP transfers ddᶜ from g to u−ψ. The resulting signed insertion is the difference of two (d+1)-fold products, both zero. Its preceding current has bidegree (n−1,n−1) and is admissible, also when d=0 and it is smooth. Thus energy is representative independent in every mixed factor. Decomposing any smooth closed real factor η as (η+AΩ)−AΩ, both Kähler, gives a well-defined symmetric functional ℓ_u on Sym^m H^(1,1)(X,R), independent of representatives, decompositions and bases. Its diagonal is the degree-m energy polynomial. A simultaneous θ→θ+ddᶜg, (u,ψ)→(u−g,ψ−g) leaves currents and differences unchanged.

At positive ε the exact bounded expansion is E_ψ^(n,ε,ω)(u)=Σ_(k≤d)binom(n,k)ε^(n−k)E_ψ^(k,ω)(u). The coefficient identity Σ_j binom(j,a)binom(n−j,k−a)=binom(n+1,k+1) counts subsets by their (a+1)-st element. Lower coefficients satisfy |E^(k)|≤‖u−ψ‖∞M_k. For arbitrary Kähler representatives whose classes converge to a Kähler λ, class-polynomial mass bounds suppress all k<d terms after division by binom(n,d)ε^m, leaving E_ψ,λ(u). Uniformly approaching bounded-type perturbed potentials have error at most their supremum error times the actual anchor mass, so the same limit holds. No class-volume equality or zero-volume probability normalization is used. This reconstructed bounded theorem is supporting material, not original-atom closure.

The expanded reconstruction and all indispensable literal source bodies are in P15.1-argument.md; standalone P15.1-partial.tex and PDF contain the full authored proof. Source auditing and rerun commands are recorded in n4.

notes.summary: Proves auxiliary-independent full-mass and genuine F1 domains for a fixed actual type, with full finite-energy truncation/cocycle reconstruction.
notes.detailedSummary: Scalar DDNL deficits against omega1^j(A omega0-omega1)^(m-j) are nonnegative and sum to zero, proving common full mass across all auxiliary forms/classes, including d=0. Positive fixed-form comparison gives common joint linear finiteness. Convexity yields all mixed full masses and mixed-weight integrability; exact locality plus equal mass yields truncation identities, finite energy equivalence, decreasing continuity, concavity, unbounded cocycle, anchor and gauge invariance. The domain contains an explicit unbounded P1xP1 potential. No uncontrolled moving-form perturbation extension is made.
notes.text:
Use n1's setting and checked foundations. The following proves common domains for every fixed smooth Kähler auxiliary form/class, including d=0.

Define E_ψ(ω)={u∈PSH(X,θ):u≤ψ+C and ∫⟨T_u^d⟩ω^m=∫⟨P^d⟩ω^m}. Suppose equality holds for ω₀. Given ω₁ choose A so D=Aω₀−ω₁ is Kähler. For j=0,…,m define scalar Δ_j=∫(⟨P^d⟩−⟨T_u^d⟩)ω₁^jD^(m−j). DDNL Theorem 2.4 applies with d θ-slots, ψ less singular than u, j smooth ω₁-slots and m−j smooth D-slots, zero potentials on both sides in the smooth slots. All backgrounds are pseudoeffective and all potentials are psh in their stated backgrounds. Thus Δ_j≥0. Expansion gives Σ_j binom(m,j)Δ_j=A^m∫(⟨P^d⟩−⟨T_u^d⟩)ω₀^m=0. Every Δ_j is zero, particularly Δ_m. Reversing forms proves a common E_ψ. No positivity of a difference current is assumed. At d=0 both products are 1 and all deficits vanish identically. Applying this equality to Σt_iω_i for t_i>0 and comparing polynomial coefficients also proves full-mass equality against every mixed product of m Kähler forms.

Define F¹_ψ by u∈E_ψ and Σ_(a=0)^d binom(d,a)∫|u−ψ|⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m<∞ for one ω. For two fixed Kähler forms cω₀≤ω₁≤Cω₀, positive powers give measure inequalities c^mQω₀^m≤Qω₁^m≤C^mQω₀^m for every positive mixed d-current Q. Integrating the nonnegative weight proves equivalent finiteness for every auxiliary class/form, and likewise for mixed complementary Kähler factors. Constants change weights by bounded amounts against finite measures and do not affect membership. At d=0 this is ordinary quasi-psh L¹ integrability against smooth volume, and full mass is automatic.

The additional external theorem is Vu arXiv:2005.13241v3 Section 3, Theorem 3.4: diagonal relative full-mass and diagonal joint χ-energy classes are convex for a common positive reference P in a pseudoeffective class, a closed positive relative current R, and convex increasing χ with χ(−∞)=−∞. Our application has d≥1 product factors, R=ω^m smooth, χ(t)=t, and top degree; connectedness identifies cohomology equality with total-mass equality. Normalizing u≤ψ and source potentials negative, its Definition (3.1) is exactly (d/2)Σ_a binom(d,a)∫(ψ−u)⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m, since Vu potentials are halved. Thus its finiteness is precisely our definition. At d=0 we use direct integrability, not that positive-factor theorem. Convexity holds in both cases.

For normalized u_i≤ψ in the full-mass domain, convexity makes w=N⁻¹Σu_i full mass. Its degree-d mass is the average of N^d ordered mixed masses, each nonnegative and at most M_d by DDNL with d current and m smooth slots. Equality of their average forces every mixed mass to equal M_d. This holds for all auxiliary powers and hence, by polynomial extraction, all mixed complementary factors. If u_i lie in F¹, weighted convexity makes w finite energy; the a=d weighted term of w and positive expansion make ψ−w integrable against each ordered mixed product. Since 0≤ψ−u_i≤N(ψ−w), all family differences are integrable against every such product. At d=0 use smooth L¹. This proves all mixed finiteness needed below.

For u≤ψ, put z=ψ−u, u_L=max(u,ψ−L), μ_a=⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m and μ_a,L=⟨T_(u_L)^aP^(d−a)⟩ω^m. Both measures have mass M_d and agree on G_L={u>ψ−L}. The exact external locality used here is Vu v3 Theorem 3.3: bounded local psh product factors equal on intersections of strict comparisons of possibly unbounded psh comparison potentials give equal restricted products. Our applications FIRST truncate every local product potential and intersect G_L with their simultaneous strict finite truncation loci, apply the bounded-factor theorem, and exhaust those loci using the defining BEGZ restrictions. Poles are uncharged. We do not assert an unbounded-factor version. On B_L=X minus G_L the truncated weight is L. Equal mass and equality on G_L imply μ_a,L(B_L)=μ_a(B_L), hence
∫(ψ−u_L)dμ_a,L=∫min(z,L)dμ_a.
Boundary equality points have weight L and cause no problem. This identity also holds with fixed mixed complementary factors. Monotone convergence proves that E_ψ,λ(u_L) decreases to the finite mixed-integral energy E_ψ,λ(u). Conversely on E_ψ the truncation limit is finite exactly when every nonnegative ∫z dμ_a is finite, equivalently joint linear finiteness. This proves a genuine finite-energy definition. Mixed masses give E(u+c)=E(u)+cM_d; for u≤ψ+C, writing u_L=(u−C)_(L+C)+C proves the same truncation limit.

Here is the complete continuity/tail argument. For bounded-type v_j↓v with |v_j−ψ|≤B uniformly, the mixed measures have exactly their limit's mass by DDNL. Use η_A=min(1,max(ψ+A,0)). On its nonzero locus truncate every local psh product factor below a uniform bound depending on A,B. Factors and the bounded weights η_A(v_j−ψ) are uniformly bounded, quasicontinuous, and converge in capacity. DDNL Proposition 2.2 applies to these bounded local factors in every slot, with smooth factors filling to n. The capacity facts are GZ, J. Geom. Anal. 15 (2005), Proposition 3.7 for BOUNDED decreasing potentials, Proposition 3.6's O(1/A) sublevel bound, Proposition 3.10 local/global capacity comparison and Corollary 3.8 quasicontinuity. For general decreasing quasi-psh functions choose a dominating Kähler background, apply bounded 3.7 to max(f_j,−A), discard {f<−A+1} using 3.6, and then send A→∞. Thus no unbounded hypothesis is falsely attributed to 3.7. Local bounded convergence and a partition of unity give convergence of the η_A-weighted integrals. The omitted absolute weight is at most B times the omitted mass. First send j→∞, then A→∞; the limit measure has no mass on ψ's poles. This proves bounded decreasing energy continuity.

For general F¹ v_j↓u with u in F¹, monotonicity sandwiches E(u)≤E(v_j)≤E(max(v_j,ψ−L)). At fixed L use the bounded lemma, then send L→∞ using the exact truncation identity. This proves all asserted decreasing continuity. Convexity and the decreasing bounded approximations (1−t)u_L+t v_L transfer bounded concavity to F¹.

For u,v≤ψ, their simultaneous mixed truncation measures have mass M_d and agree on G_L={u>ψ−L}∩{v>ψ−L}. Their complementary masses agree. On B_L, |u_L−v_L|≤L and L μ_L(B_L)=L μ(B_L)≤∫_(B_L)((ψ−u)+(ψ−v))dμ→0 by the mixed integrability proved above. The original |u−v| tail also tends to zero. Therefore the bounded cocycle passes termwise to the finite identity E_ψ(u)−E_ψ(v)=(d+1)⁻¹Σ_a∫(u−v)⟨T_u^aT_v^(d−a)⟩ω^m. Constants and d=0 are handled by the equal mixed masses and direct smooth integration.

If χ∈C_ψ, full mass and domination up to constants coincide. χ itself lies in F¹_ψ; the mixed-family integrability argument gives finiteness of |u−χ| against all products with χ. Reversing anchors proves F¹_χ=F¹_ψ. The cocycle gives E_χ(u)=E_ψ(u)−E_ψ(χ). Representative independence follows by applying n1 to every u_L and taking their exact limits; theta gauge invariance follows from unchanged currents and differences.

The domain truly contains unbounded differences: on P¹×P¹ take θ=p₁*κ, ψ=0, ∫κ=1, and v(z)=−b(−log|z|)^a near zero, 0<a<1/2. A smooth annular cutoff and sufficiently small b make κ+ddᶜv positive globally. Its singular radial Hessian is positive, its flux is proportional to (−log r)^(a−1)→0, so it has no point atom and has mass one by distributional Stokes. Smooth-volume integrability is exponential in −log r; weighted current integrability is ∫^∞s^(2a−2)ds<∞. Thus u=p₁*v has full degree-one mass and finite F¹ energy but is unbounded. No fibration is assumed in the theorem. No uncontrolled moving-form perturbation extension follows.

notes.summary: Proves coefficientwise polynomial extension and the exact finite-dimensional minimum energy-family reference on the entire common F1 domain.
notes.detailedSummary: Finitely many Kähler powers span Sym^m H^(1,1), giving unisolvent evaluations. Finite truncation values at those classes force coefficientwise convergence for every F1 potential. Explicit mixed integral functionals are representative independent, and all unbounded functionals span exactly the bounded S. Two Kähler references give every anchored F1 energy equally iff their m-powers agree in Q=Sym^m V/Ann(S). Constants retain the positive raw-mass polynomial; bounded-equivalent anchors and theta gauges preserve S/K/domain. Universal factorization, quotient topology and decreasing coefficient continuity are proved. This is family-relative minimality, not a universal geometric classification or lower-dimensional carrier theorem.
notes.text:
Use n1 and n2. Put V=H^(1,1)(X,R), B=Sym^mV, m=n−d≥1. For bounded-type u, define
ℓ_u^ψ(λ₁⊙⋯⊙λ_m)=(d+1)⁻¹Σ_a∫(u−ψ)⟨T_u^aP^(d−a)⟩η₁⋯η_m,
where η_i are arbitrary smooth closed real representatives of λ_i. n1 proves representative independence with bounded admissible IBP and degree-(d+1) vanishing, then extends by differences of Kähler forms. Its diagonal polynomial is the anchored energy.

The powers λ^⊙m for Kähler λ span B. Otherwise a nonzero dual functional annihilating their span would define a homogeneous polynomial zero on the nonempty open Kähler cone. A polynomial zero on an open box is zero: apply one-variable coefficient uniqueness in each coordinate successively. In a basis e_i its x^β coefficient is (m!/β!)ℓ(e₁^⊙β₁⋯e_h^⊙β_h), so all coefficients zero imply the functional zero, a contradiction. Choose N=dim B powers forming a basis. Evaluation at these N Kähler classes is therefore a linear isomorphism B*→R^N; this proves existence of an unisolvent set without auxiliary choices entering the answer.

For every u∈F¹_ψ, n2 gives finite convergence E_ψ,λ_i(u_L)→E_ψ,λ_i(u) at those classes. Applying the inverse evaluation isomorphism forces coefficientwise ℓ_(u_L)→ℓ_u in B*. At every other Kähler λ, evaluation continuity and n2's truncation identity imply E_ψ,λ(u)=ℓ_u(λ^⊙m). Uniqueness on the open cone makes this independent of all bases, unisolvent sets and decreasing bounded-type approximations. Explicitly ℓ_u has the same mixed-integral formula above: with mixed complementary Kähler W, the equal-mass locality proof gives each weighted truncation identity and its integral convergence; decompose arbitrary η_i into differences of Kähler forms, expand finitely, and pass every integral to the limit. Each absolute integral is finite by domination by a multiple of a fixed Kähler m-power. This proves representative independence without unbounded IBP. Polarization is ℓ_u(λ₁⊙⋯⊙λ_m)=(m!)⁻¹Σ_J(−1)^(m−|J|)p_u(Σ_(j∈J)λ_j), where p_u is the unique polynomial on V. Expansion proves the formula by cancelling terms missing a variable. Non-Kähler polynomial arguments are algebraic extensions, not positive auxiliary references.

Define S=span{ℓ_u:u∈C_ψ}, K=Ann(S), Q=B/K and q:B→Q. Finite-dimensional S is closed, so every unbounded coefficient limit belongs to S. Conversely C_ψ⊂F¹_ψ. Hence the unbounded functional span is exactly S and its common kernel exactly K. Therefore two Kähler classes give the same anchored energy for EVERY u∈F¹_ψ if and only if q(λ₀^⊙m)=q(λ₁^⊙m): equality on bounded potentials annihilates S, and membership of all unbounded functionals in S proves the reverse implication. This is the necessary/sufficient whole-domain minimum-reference result.

The raw-mass functional M(λ₁⊙⋯⊙λ_m)=∫⟨P^d⟩η₁⋯η_m is representative independent by closedness and Stokes and positive on Kähler powers. Mixed mass equality proves ℓ_(ψ+c)=cM and ℓ_(u+c)=ℓ_u+cM. In particular M∈S and K⊂ker M, so the quotient retains raw mass and has positive dimension; there is no probability normalization. For χ∈C_ψ, n2 gives the same domain and anchored cocycle. Equality on the Kähler cone and polarization yield ℓ_u^χ=ℓ_u^ψ−ℓ_χ^ψ. Since ℓ_ψ^χ=−ℓ_χ^ψ, the two spans, kernels and quotients are identical. The anchor fixes the origin rather than disappearing. Simultaneous smooth theta gauge changes preserve every current, difference, truncation and functional; any smooth representative change of α has this gauge by the exact DGMS lemma in n1.

The precise universal factorization is as follows. The all-energy map t↦(ℓ_u(t))_(u∈F¹) has kernel K, so Q identifies with its finite-dimensional output space. If a linear descriptor r:B→R₀ lets every ℓ_u factor through r by a linear functional, then ker r⊂K and there is a unique surjective linear map r(B)→Q, r(t)↦q(t). For actual auxiliaries use I={q(λ^⊙m):λ Kähler}⊂Q. Any set-valued descriptor on the Kähler cone determining every energy must map onto I by the same equality criterion. Conversely I suffices. This is family-relative minimum information, not an independently geometric kernel theorem; I need not be a vector space, manifold, or all of Q.

Give I the subspace topology from finite-dimensional Q. Each descended ℓ_u is continuous. Choosing bounded u₁,…,u_s whose ℓ's form a basis of S makes their energy coordinates Q→R^s a linear isomorphism; convergence of those finitely many energies is exactly quotient convergence. If u_j↓u in F¹, decreasing continuity at the unisolvent classes gives coefficient convergence ℓ_(u_j)→ℓ_u, hence uniform polynomial convergence on compact subsets of V and functional convergence on bounded subsets of Q. Simultaneously τ_j→τ in I therefore gives ℓ_(u_j)(τ_j)→ℓ_u(τ). This does not imply a rescaled top-energy limit for moving rough auxiliary forms.

In the P¹×P¹ smooth-reference example V has the two pullback generators a,b; the product cell structure has two real 2-cells and no odd cells, and fiber evaluations identify these generators. Kähler classes are Aa+Bb with A,B>0. Every θ-psh potential is constant on the second-factor fibers by the compact-curve psh maximum principle, or identically minus infinity on such a fiber, so u=p₁*v. For bounded u the energy is (B/2)∫v((κ+ddᶜv)+κ). Thus all functionals span precisely the B coordinate, constants supplying it. Q=R with q(Aa+Bb)=B, I=(0,∞); the span theorem extends this computation to the whole genuine F¹ domain.

The required retained data for this family are X, α, actual bounded comparison type and its actual degree, an anchor, and τ∈I. Theta is a smooth gauge coordinate. Integrals are carried by the n-dimensional X with current bidegree (d,d). The quotient does not supply a geometric d-dimensional carrier, a numerical-dimension theorem or universal classification. Original P15.1 is not claimed solved.

notes.summary: Reconstructs the same-class unbounded concentration counterexample, records actual-degree/class-volume mismatch, and leaves original P15.1 partial.
notes.detailedSummary: On P1xP1 a full degree-one F1 potential with radial exponent 0<a<1/2 has finite full relative top energy at every positive perturbation. Smooth fixed-class auxiliary bump forms at radius exp(-epsilon^(-2/a)) force the rescaled top energy to minus infinity, while a fixed form yields the finite degree-one value. Thus n3 quotient continuity cannot imply the refuted joint perturbation assertion. A divisor reference in the same nef class has actual d=0 although the numerical dimension is one, and actual versus class-volume leading exponents differ. Full original path/minimum-reference closure remains unproved. Audit records source pins, exact finite diagnostics and twice-compiled document as observations, not mathematical certification.
notes.text:
Use n1–n3. The supplied concentration obstruction is reconstructed analytically rather than assumed. On X=P¹×P¹, θ=p₁*κ, ψ=0, take n2's u=p₁*v, v=−b(−log|z|)^a−c near zero, 0<a<1/2 and c≥0. It has degree-one full mass and finite F¹ energy. Its class is nef and has volume zero because θ²=0 and the nef positive product is cup product.

For small ε let ρ_ε=exp(−ε^(−2/a)) and choose a smooth nonnegative area bump β_ε of integral one supported in |z|<ρ_ε. Put κ_ε=(κ+β_ε)/2 and ω_ε=p₁*κ_ε+p₂*κ. These are smooth Kähler forms; all [κ_ε]=[κ] because integration identifies H²(P¹,R), so all [ω_ε] equal the same Kähler class. The potential is exactly u at every parameter. For each fixed ε, v is integrable against κ_ε (smooth bounded density), κ and S=κ+ddᶜv. All weighted top terms are finite.

Writing U=p₁*S, A=p₁*κ, B=p₂*κ and A_ε=p₁*κ_ε, the three top products are respectively 2ε(A+εA_ε)B, ε(U+A+2εA_ε)B and 2ε(U+εA_ε)B. This follows off the polar fiber by wedge multiplication; horizontal squares vanish, and nonpluripolar extension adds no pole mass. Both actual top masses are 2ε(1+ε), so u has full perturbed top mass. Direct summation of the three finite weighted integrals gives
E₀^(2,ε,ω_ε)(u)/(2ε)=E₀,λ(u)+ε∫vκ_ε,
where E₀,λ(u)=(1/2)∫v(S+κ) is finite. On the bump support −v≥bε⁻², so ∫vκ_ε≤−(b/2)ε⁻² and the rescaled expression tends to minus infinity. The fixed smooth product form gives a fixed finite lower integral and limit E₀,λ(u). Thus even identical potential, class and quotient reference, with finite full perturbed top energy at every parameter, do not imply the unrestricted unbounded moving-representative assertion. This does not contradict the degree-d polynomial/quotient continuity theorem.

Actual degree is also distinct from class numerical dimension. In the same class the logarithmic reference g=log(|z|²/(1+|z|²)), pulled back to X, has current the vertical divisor: ddᶜlog|z|²=δ₀ follows from flux 4π and our normalization, while ddᶜlog(1+|z|²)=κ. Its nonpluripolar first product is zero, so d=0, although the nef class has numerical dimension one by its nonzero first cup trace and zero square. For ω=Ap₁*κ+Bp₂*κ, actual perturbed reference mass is 2ABε² but class volume is 2Bε+2ABε². Their leading exponents differ; constant-shift actual energy is c times actual mass. No replacement by a class-volume leading coefficient is justified.

The new results are proposals 1–3 in the stipulated actual-type scope: common auxiliary-independent full mass and genuine F¹, coefficientwise polynomial extension, and exact whole-domain minimum energy-family quotient retaining raw mass. Original P15.1 remains partial. The minimum is relative to this prescribed family, not an independently geometric universal minimum for every possible theory. The carrier remains X of dimension n, with no geometric d-dimensional carrier or general geometric kernel characterization. Unrestricted moving-form limits are refuted, while general moving unbounded-potential/joint limits, lower-degree weighted controls in arbitrary reference settings, increasing continuity and unbounded differential/path calculus remain unproved. An iterated bounded-leading-limit then truncation-limit prescription follows from the proved identities, but equality with every joint/reversed limit is not asserted.
